summary: Yin Shun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, National Taiwan Normal University, and Taisho University, learning under Daxing, Taixu, and Fazun. He held posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Shandao Temple, and Hong Kong Buddhist Association.
Ying Zhu is a scholar in history, archaeology, and sinology who earned a PhD at the Georgia Institute of Technology, studying with committee member Eugene Y. Wang.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) worked in sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Kansai University, and Harvard University. He held positions at the University of Michigan, Yale University, and Princeton University.
Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Nordan Hutuktu in 1926 and Bai Puren in 1929.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) worked in history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fudan, Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Zurich, Paris Institute of Political Studies, and Harvard. He held posts at Tsinghua University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University.
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (c. 2008–2013) under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yiu-ming Fung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong by 1984 and served as Acting Head of the Division of Humanities at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology until 2005.
Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University and taught Eastern philosophy at the University of Haifa.

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University and as a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Yoichi Fukuda (born 1957) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (c. 1982–1986) and as a professor at Otani University (c. 1999–2003).
Yoichi Kaji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an associate professor at Otani University Junior College until 2002 and as a professor at Otani University around 2002.
Yong Hua Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College by 2014 under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar and teacher. He studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Yongshan He is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at McMaster University (c. 2005–2011) under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn, as well as Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University (c. 1912–1917) and Harvard University (c. 1919–1922), later holding a post in Peking University's Philosophy Department from 1940 to 1949.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies from c. 1980 to 1998.

Yoshiaki Kandate is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia and the University of Chicago, and held a professorship at Shiga University of Medical Science.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe. He held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, Kobe Women's University, Otani University, and Anshin-in.
Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned a doctorate at Komazawa University and served there as a lecturer from c. 1972 to 1977.
Yoshihiko Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held positions as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, board chairman at Kongojushinkai, and director of psychological services at Kongoju.
